learn.title: Shared responsibility model and IaaS / PaaS / SaaS
objectives: Explain which security and management tasks belong to the customer, to Microsoft, or to both.
Read the responsibility matrix layer by layer for on-premises, IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.
Define IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, with their advantages and trade-offs.
Pick the right service type for a scenario and name an Azure or Microsoft example of each.
concepts: Security and management duties are split between the cloud provider and the customer. The split changes with the service type.
Information and data, devices (mobile and PCs), and accounts and identities, in every model.
Physical hosts, the physical network and the physical datacenter.
Identity and directory infrastructure, applications, network controls and the operating system.
The provider supplies virtual machines, storage and networking on its hardware. You manage the OS, middleware, runtime, apps and data. Most control and most work. Example: Azure Virtual Machines.
The provider manages the infrastructure, OS and runtime. You manage your application and data. Faster development, less control. Examples: Azure App Service, Azure SQL Database.
Complete software delivered over the internet. The provider runs everything. You manage data, users, devices and settings. Examples: Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365.
Often treated as an extension of PaaS: event-driven code with no server management, such as Azure Functions.
The customer is responsible for every layer, from the building up to the data.
comparisons: IaaS: customer. PaaS: Microsoft. SaaS: Microsoft.
IaaS: customer. PaaS: shared. SaaS: Microsoft.
IaaS: customer. PaaS: shared. SaaS: shared.
IaaS: most control, most effort. PaaS: balanced. SaaS: least control, least effort.
IaaS: install anything. PaaS: supported runtimes only. SaaS: use the app as provided.
traps: In SaaS you still own your data, accounts and devices.
In PaaS you don't patch the operating system, but you do secure your application code and configuration.
Identity and directory infrastructure is shared in both PaaS and SaaS, not Microsoft-only.
Physical security is never the customer's job in Azure, even with IaaS.
A managed database such as Azure SQL Database is PaaS, while SQL Server on a VM is IaaS.
revision: Data, devices and identities: always you.
Physical hosts, network and datacenter: always Microsoft.
The OS moves to Microsoft as soon as you leave IaaS.
Applications and network controls: shared in PaaS, Microsoft in SaaS.
IaaS = rent infrastructure. PaaS = rent a platform for your code. SaaS = rent finished software.
Anchor examples: VMs (IaaS), App Service / SQL Database (PaaS), Microsoft 365 (SaaS).

questions.q: What does the shared responsibility model describe?
opts: How security and management duties are divided between the cloud provider and the customer
How many customers share one physical server
How data is replicated between two regions
How cloud costs are split between departments
questions.e: The model defines who secures and manages each layer (physical, OS, network controls, applications, identities, data). The split changes with IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

questions.q: Employees access Microsoft 365 from personal laptops and phones. Who is responsible for securing those devices?
Which layer of the shared responsibility model is always the customer's responsibility, whatever the service type?
In Azure, who is responsible for the physical hosts that virtual machines run on?
In a traditional on-premises datacenter, who is responsible for every layer, from physical security to data?
opts: The organisation that owns the datacenter
questions.e: On-premises, the organisation owns the whole stack. Moving to the cloud hands some layers to the provider.

questions.q: Which description fits infrastructure as a service (IaaS)?
opts: The provider supplies complete applications ready for end users
The provider manages the OS and runtime, and the customer deploys only code
The provider supplies virtual machines, storage and networking, and the customer manages the operating system and everything above it
The customer buys and installs physical servers in the provider's building

questions.q: Which description fits platform as a service (PaaS)?
opts: Dedicated physical servers leased by the month
A managed environment where the provider handles infrastructure, OS and runtime, and the customer builds and runs its applications
Finished software that users simply sign in to
Raw virtual machines that the customer fully configures

questions.q: Which description fits software as a service (SaaS)?
opts: A platform for deploying custom code
Virtual machines rented by the hour
Complete applications hosted and managed by the provider, which users access over the internet
A toolkit for building operating systems

questions.q: Which Azure service is an example of PaaS for databases?
opts: SQL Server installed on an Azure virtual machine
questions.e: Azure SQL Database is a managed relational database, so Microsoft handles the OS, patching and backups. SQL Server on a VM is IaaS.

questions.q: A sales team uses Dynamics 365 in a browser to manage customer relationships. Which service type is this?
Which option is an IaaS offering?

questions.q: Which cloud service type gives the customer the most control over the computing environment?

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: Which cloud service type requires the least management effort from the customer?
True or false: 'With SaaS, the customer has no responsibilities at all.'
opts: True, as long as the app has an SLA
True. The provider handles every layer
False. The customer must patch the SaaS operating system
False. The customer still manages its data, devices, and accounts and identities

questions.q: Who maintains the physical network cabling and switches inside Azure datacenters?
opts: Each customer for its own traffic

questions.q: A web app runs on Azure App Service. Who is responsible for the operating system of the underlying servers?
opts: The customer's developers, through deployment scripts
Shared equally between customer and Microsoft

questions.q: A company runs workloads on Azure VMs. Who is responsible for configuring which inbound ports are open, for example through network security groups?
opts: Nobody, because Azure blocks all ports by default and they can't be changed
questions.e: Network controls are the customer's in IaaS, shared in PaaS, and Microsoft's in SaaS.

questions.q: For a SaaS application such as Microsoft 365, who is primarily responsible for the network controls that protect the service itself?
opts: Shared equally between the customer and Microsoft

questions.q: According to the shared responsibility model, how is responsibility for applications handled in PaaS?
opts: Microsoft alone, including the customer's code
It's shared: the provider runs the platform, and the customer secures its own application code and configuration
The customer alone, including the platform
Nobody, because PaaS applications are self-securing

questions.q: In SaaS, how is responsibility for identity and directory infrastructure split?
opts: It's shared between the customer and the provider
questions.e: The provider runs the identity platform, while the customer configures users, groups and settings such as MFA.

questions.q: An attacker signs in to a company's Microsoft 365 tenant using a stolen password because MFA was never enabled. Under the shared responsibility model, whose responsibility was that protection?
opts: The customer's, because accounts and identities always belong to the customer
Microsoft's, because SaaS security is entirely the provider's

questions.q: A company stores files in Azure Blob Storage. Who decides which files are confidential and who should be able to read them?
opts: Azure automatically, with no customer input

questions.q: A storage container was accidentally configured to allow anonymous public read access, and confidential data leaked. Which statement is correct?
opts: This can't happen in Azure, because anonymous access isn't possible
This is a customer configuration issue, because data and access settings are the customer's responsibility
This happened because the physical datacenter was breached
This is Microsoft's fault, because Microsoft secures all storage
questions.e: Microsoft secures the platform, but how you configure access to your data is your responsibility.

questions.q: A company installs a third-party web server on an Azure VM. Who must apply security updates to that web server software?
A team hosts a Node.js API on a PaaS service. A security patch is released for the underlying web server platform. Who typically applies it?
opts: The end users of the API
The cloud provider, as part of managing the platform
Nobody, because PaaS platforms never need patching
The team, by logging on to each server

questions.q: What is a key advantage of IaaS over PaaS?
opts: Lower management effort for the customer
No need to manage the operating system
Full control over the operating system and installed software

questions.q: What is a key advantage of PaaS for developers?
opts: They don't need to write any application code
They can install any custom kernel drivers
They can focus on writing code while the platform handles servers, OS updates and much of the scaling
They get full administrative access to the host OS

questions.q: What is a typical limitation of PaaS compared with IaaS?
opts: Less control over the underlying environment, for example only supported runtimes and configurations are available
You must patch the operating system yourself
You can't deploy your own code

questions.q: What is a common trade-off of choosing SaaS?
opts: The need to manage virtual machines
Limited ability to customise how the software works internally

questions.q: A small charity needs email and document collaboration within a week and has no IT staff. Which service type suits it best?

questions.q: A company has written its own web application and wants to deploy it quickly, with automatic scaling and no server maintenance. Which service type fits best?

questions.q: A company wants a relational database for a new app, with automated backups and patching, and without managing any servers. What should it choose?
opts: SQL Server on an Azure virtual machine
A Linux VM with a manually installed database engine
An Excel file stored in OneDrive

questions.q: Serverless computing, such as Azure Functions, is most closely related to which service type?
questions.e: Serverless extends PaaS: the provider manages servers, and you supply only code that runs in response to events.

questions.q: A web app on App Service is breached through an SQL-injection flaw in the company's own code. Who was responsible for preventing this?
opts: The customer, because the application code is theirs
Microsoft, because App Service is PaaS

questions.q: In PaaS, which of the following is NOT the customer's responsibility?
In IaaS, which of the following is NOT Microsoft's responsibility?
opts: Configuring the guest operating system firewall

questions.q: An employee's unencrypted laptop holding synced company files is stolen. Under the shared responsibility model, whose responsibility was securing that laptop?
opts: Microsoft's, because the files came from the cloud
The airline where it was lost
The cloud provider and the laptop maker jointly

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: A company runs a web app on IaaS VMs and spends hours each month patching them. Which change would most reduce this work while keeping its own code?
opts: Move the app to a PaaS service such as Azure App Service
Add more VMs to spread the patching
Move the VMs to larger sizes
Switch to a SaaS product and abandon the code

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: How is SaaS usually paid for, compared with IaaS?
opts: SaaS is free, and IaaS is per user
SaaS always requires buying hardware, and IaaS is per user
SaaS is usually a subscription per user or per licence, while IaaS is usually billed by resource consumption
Both are always one-time perpetual licences

questions.q:
Evaluate these statements.
1. In IaaS, the customer is responsible for network controls.
2. In PaaS, Microsoft is responsible for the operating system.
3. In SaaS, the customer is responsible for the physical datacenter.
Which statements are true?

Evaluate these statements about responsibilities that never transfer to the provider.
1. Information and data.
2. Devices such as mobile phones and PCs.
3. Operating system.
Which are always the customer's responsibility?

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: A company runs a legacy app on Azure VMs, a new API on Azure App Service, and uses Microsoft 365 for email. For which of these must it patch the operating system itself?
opts: Only the legacy app on Azure VMs
questions.e: OS patching is the customer's job only in IaaS.

questions.q: In PaaS, which layer is shared between the customer and Microsoft, rather than being entirely one party's job?

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: A firm needs a payroll solution. It has no developers, wants the vendor to handle updates and compliance features, and accepts limited customisation. What should it choose?
opts: Payroll software installed on IaaS VMs
A payroll app it builds on PaaS

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: A development team needs to run a custom app built on a niche language runtime that no PaaS service supports. It still wants to avoid buying hardware. What fits best?
opts: Azure Functions on the Consumption plan

questions.q: A company moves its on-premises file server to SharePoint Online, a SaaS service. Which responsibility moves from the company to Microsoft?
opts: Protecting user accounts with strong authentication
Maintaining the server operating system and application software
Deciding who can access each file

questions.q: For a SaaS application, which task remains with the customer?
opts: Assigning licences and permissions to users

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares SQL Server on an Azure VM with Azure SQL Database?
opts: Both are SaaS, so Microsoft handles everything
SQL Server on a VM is IaaS and the customer patches the OS and database engine; Azure SQL Database is PaaS and Microsoft handles that patching
Both are IaaS, so the customer patches both
SQL Server on a VM is PaaS, and Azure SQL Database is IaaS

questions.q: True or false: 'In PaaS, network controls are entirely Microsoft's responsibility.'
opts: False. In PaaS, network controls are shared between the customer and Microsoft
True. The customer has no network settings in PaaS
False. They're entirely the customer's responsibility

questions.q: What does IaaS stand for?
What does PaaS stand for?
How do users typically access a SaaS application?
opts: Through a web browser or a client app, without installing or managing any servers
By uploading the source code to a PaaS platform
By installing it on a physical server they own
By deploying it onto their own virtual machines

questions.q: When a company creates an Azure virtual machine, who chooses the VM size (CPU and memory)?
In IaaS, who decides which operating system image a virtual machine uses?
Who is responsible for the power, cooling and fire suppression in Azure datacenters?
opts: Shared equally between the customer and Microsoft

questions.q: A company runs an application on an Azure VM. Who is responsible for making sure the application's data is backed up, for example by configuring Azure Backup?
opts: Nobody, because VMs can't lose data
questions.e: Azure provides backup tools, but in IaaS it's up to the customer to configure and verify backups of their data.

questions.q: Which service type is closest to 'renting the hardware and building on it yourself'?
In the popular 'pizza as a service' analogy, eating at a restaurant, where everything is made and served for you, corresponds to which cloud service type?
In which service type does the customer install and manage middleware and runtimes, such as a web server or language runtime?
opts: None of the cloud service types

questions.q: Which is a common benefit of SaaS for customers?
opts: Customers can modify the provider's source code
The software is kept up to date by the provider, without customers installing upgrades
Customers control the server operating system

questions.q: A SaaS application is described as multitenant. What does this mean?
opts: Only one customer can use the application at a time
Customers must host the application on their own servers
Each customer gets its own physical datacenter
Many customer organisations use the same application service, with each customer's data kept isolated

questions.q: Which of these is delivered as SaaS?
opts: The Power BI service for sharing reports in a browser

questions.q: Who chooses the Azure region where a customer's resources and data are stored?
opts: The region is always the one closest to Microsoft headquarters

questions.q: Who creates and manages role assignments that control which employees can manage resources in a company's Azure subscription?
opts: The resources assign roles to themselves

questions.q: A company running Azure VMs asks who patches the hypervisor and host software underneath its VMs. What is the answer?
opts: Microsoft, as part of maintaining the physical hosts
Shared, with the customer approving each patch
Nobody, because hypervisors are never patched
The customer, from inside each VM

questions.q: A law firm must keep all emails for seven years. It uses Exchange Online. Who is responsible for configuring retention so that this requirement is met?
Who is responsible for installing and maintaining antimalware software inside a Windows Server VM running in Azure?
opts: The VM image is permanently protected with no action needed

questions.q: A company chooses customer-managed encryption keys for its Azure storage account instead of Microsoft-managed keys. Who becomes responsible for managing and rotating those keys?
opts: The keys rotate themselves and need no owner

questions.q: A company hosts its website on Azure App Service with a custom domain. Who is responsible for configuring the custom domain and its TLS certificate binding for the app?
questions.e: In PaaS the platform is Microsoft's, but the application's configuration, including domains and certificates, is the customer's.

questions.q: On a PaaS hosting service, who decides how many instances an app may scale to and under what conditions?
opts: End users, through the app's interface
The customer, by configuring scaling settings that the platform then carries out
Microsoft alone, with no customer settings

questions.q: A company runs a critical app on a single Azure VM. Who is responsible for designing the deployment so the app survives the failure of one datacenter, for example by using availability zones?
opts: Nobody, because single VMs can't fail
Microsoft, which automatically spreads single VMs across zones

questions.q: Who is responsible for keeping a SaaS application such as Microsoft 365 running and available?
Azure holds many compliance certifications. Which statement is correct?
opts: Any workload in Azure is automatically compliant with every regulation
Compliance applies only to on-premises systems
Compliance is entirely the customer's, and Microsoft holds no certifications
Microsoft's certifications cover the platform, but the customer must still use and configure services in a way that meets its own compliance obligations

questions.q: A team wants to deploy a new app version to a staging environment and then swap it into production with no downtime, without managing servers. Which service type typically provides this?
opts: PaaS, for example App Service deployment slots
IaaS, using a single virtual machine

questions.q: A company uses Azure SQL Database. Who decides which client IP addresses or networks are allowed to connect to the database?
opts: The customer, through the database's network and firewall settings
The database is always open to the whole internet

questions.q: Who is responsible for screening and controlling the staff who have physical access to Azure datacenters?
A firmware vulnerability is found in the server hardware used in Azure datacenters. Who is responsible for updating the host firmware?
opts: Customers running VMs on those hosts
Shared, with customers scheduling the updates

questions.q: A company using SharePoint Online finds that employees can share files with anyone on the internet. Whose responsibility is it to restrict external sharing settings?
In which service type does the customer usually monitor disk space and install monitoring agents inside the operating system?
opts: None, because Azure does this for every service type

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of SaaS?
opts: Full control over the application's source code and hosting environment
Access from many devices over the internet

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of IaaS?
opts: No need to maintain the operating system
Ability to scale infrastructure on demand

questions.q: True or false: 'After moving an application to PaaS, the customer no longer needs to think about application security.'
opts: True, but only for web apps
False. The customer still secures its application code, configuration, data and identities
False. The customer must also secure the physical hosts
True. PaaS includes full application security

questions.q: An App Service app goes down because of a hardware failure in the underlying Azure infrastructure. Whose responsibility is it to restore the platform?
By default, how are Azure managed disks attached to VMs protected at rest?
opts: They're encrypted only if the VM runs Linux
They're encrypted automatically with platform-managed keys
They're unencrypted until the customer installs encryption software
They're stored as plain text for performance

1. In SaaS, applications are the provider's responsibility.
2. In PaaS, identity and directory infrastructure is shared.

Which statements are true?

Which statements are true?

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: A company wants to minimise its security and maintenance burden for a CRM system, but still needs to add its own fields and approval workflows. What fits best?
opts: A SaaS CRM, such as Dynamics 365, configured with custom fields and workflows
A CRM developed on PaaS with a custom database
A CRM installed on on-premises servers
A CRM built from scratch on IaaS VMs

questions.q: When a workload moves from IaaS to PaaS, which layer changes from customer-only to shared?
questions.e: Applications and identity infrastructure also become shared, while the OS moves entirely to Microsoft.

questions.q: When a workload moves from IaaS to PaaS, which layer moves entirely from the customer to Microsoft?
When a workload moves from PaaS to SaaS, which layer moves from shared to Microsoft?
An Azure VM is compromised because RDP was open to the whole internet and the admin account had a weak password. Which statement is correct?
opts: Responsibility is split, with Microsoft owning the password policy
The customer was responsible, because both network controls and accounts are the customer's in IaaS
Microsoft was responsible, because it runs the VM host
Nobody was responsible, because RDP attacks can't be prevented

questions.on: Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type
questions.q: A company must install a compliance agent at the OS level on every web server, wants no physical hardware, and needs the number of servers to grow and shrink automatically with demand. What fits best?
opts: A PaaS hosting plan with no OS access
A fixed set of on-premises servers
IaaS virtual machines in a Virtual Machine Scale Set with autoscale

questions.q: Which statement about the shared responsibility model is incorrect?
opts: In IaaS, the customer is responsible for the operating system
In every cloud model, Microsoft is responsible for the physical datacenter
In SaaS, Microsoft is responsible for classifying the customer's data
In every model, the customer is responsible for its devices
